office_does: A King County Southwest Electoral District District Court judge hears and decides misdemeanor criminal cases, small claims, traffic cases and protection orders for a four-year term; in practice the discretion is in pretrial release, sentencing, protection orders and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: An open seat (Judge Elizabeth Stephenson is listed as retired) that skipped the primary. Renee Walls, who reports 26 years as a municipal prosecutor and 17 as a pro tem judge and lists most of the District Court bench as endorsers, faces Noel Merfeld, a children's dependency attorney and former prosecutor and public defender who campaigns on wider access to therapeutic courts.

candidates.summary: Reports 26 years as a prosecutor for South King County cities and 17 years as a judge pro tem, and is a past president of the South King County Bar Association (self-reported). Her listed endorsers include most of the District Court bench.
highlights: 26 years as a prosecutor for cities including Algona, Burien, Federal Way and Tukwila (self-reported) [S1][S3]
Judge pro tem for 17 years, per her statement [S1]
Lists endorsements from Justices Gonzalez and Whitener and Chief Presiding Judge Robertson [S4]
Campaign largely self-funded; no bar rating found [S11][S8]

safety.basis: Prosecution-only formation of 26 years; no bail, diversion or sentencing positions published beyond a youth-diversion board seat.

experience.basis: Runs on an "unmatched 26-year record" with 17 years pro tem and broad bench endorsements.

candidates.summary: Dependency attorney representing children who reports earlier work as a prosecutor in Okanogan County and a public defender in Okanogan and Snohomish counties. He publishes a detailed platform on therapeutic courts and court access.
highlights: Prosecutor, then public defender, now a children's dependency attorney (self-reported, no dates) [S3]
Says more people who could benefit from therapeutic courts should have access to them [S4]
Says he "will impose jail when the facts of an individual case show that it is necessary" [S4]
Supports considering court facilitators for self-represented litigants [S4]

safety.basis: Explicit platform to expand therapeutic-court access and treatment, with a stated willingness to jail when needed; formation spans prosecution and defense.

experience.basis: No judicial or pro tem service reported, against an opponent with 17 years pro tem; a career lawyer, so the score reflects bench profile rather than outsider rhetoric.
